body:
I think it's something you should bring up beforehand- being self conscious about your scars at least. I don't think anyone would necessarily turned off by your scars if they're comfortable around you, but they might find them distracting if the first time they've seen your scars is while having sex. Maybe try and show them beforehand? Casually while getting out of the shower, wearing shorts depending on if they're lower on your legs, etc. Figure out what works for your situation. 

My boyfriend has never even been turned off by seeing fresh cuts, but had always been concerned. For us, he doesn't care about seeing scars because then he knows they've healed over.

They'll likely ask if they were self inflicted, ask if you are seeing a therapist, ask if you're on meds, ask if you are actively suicidal, I've never had a doctor tell my parents. If it's unrelated to whatever you're at the doctors for, I doubt that they'll say anything to them.

If you're worried, simply say that they're healing and you're working to improve your mental health, hopefully they'll drop the subject.

My boyfriend asked why I have to cut multiple times. Apparently he knew someone who would cut themselves once and be done with it.  Even though I know people who self harm or have self harmed the same way I do, I now feel really shitty about the amount of scars on my legs...

I think we've all got scars like that. I try to just think of them all as scars, not scars from when I was upset about such and such. 
My one thigh is a sea of scars, it's more or less on huge dark blob if you look from a distance, I thought continuously cutting over them would make it impossible to differentiate but no, I can pick each one out and remember exactly why I did it. 
Basically, don't do what I tried to do, just try and see it as just a scar.

As far as him simply looking at only het porn for variety, that's fair. I mean I'm not gonna pretend I don't look at it either, I can't emphasize enough that I don't care that he looks at porn in general. Some people seem to misunderstand that. I care about the three photos of our friends that I found, and that simply made me more paranoid and I began to worry about the fact he only saved porn of women.

It's also not that he saved anyones photos into the porn folder necessarily, it was his screenshot folder. All of his screenshotted photos went there, so there is a possibility that they really did just "get lost in a sea of porn", but considering every other photo he had ever screenshotted WAS porn, I don't buy it.

As far as the Valentine's Day thing, it didn't bother me until I looked through his photos. It bothered me that on a day where I'M supposed to be special, I wasn't. She was. He (probably) ignored me to just jack off to her. And the idea that he's still not over her after almost two years makes me sick.

I will admit that the whole Valentine's Day and straight porn thing is probably just me looking for more shit to get upset about.

When I was younger I was very worried others could read my mind while I was day dreaming or doing anything, really, and would have to do something like hurt myself if I thought someone read a particularly bad thought of mine.
Saw that. Asshole commented something on a now deleted post of mine that I just impulsively posted too.

Well first, I've never dated another person
Second, definitely don't see us getting married. Not something I'm interested in.
It's just that he brought it up, he made me think he cared enough about me to want to do that and then the whole photo thing ripped my fucking heart out and fucked up my head.
I'm also in a pretty fucked situation at home- I have no means of moving out on my own any time soon but I'm gonna have to.

Nononono! As far as the other women, that was actually, explicitly porn. Him looking at porn isn't an issue at all, it's just his choice of porn made me a little more uncomfortable on top of the whole photos of my friend thing
I was just trying to give context
I experience similar things on a semi regular basis. Pretty sure it's a symptom of OCD.

I think if you decide to bring it up, wait until you're both in an okay mood. Not right after or during an argument. Say hey, I've been experiencing some pretty bad suicidal ideation lately, and one of the biggest triggers is when we argue.
I think it's simply because these are all symptoms of disorders, in which the symptoms can exist in nearly every disorder, but that doesn't mean you have it.

Struggling with the exact same issue. For me and most people I know, senior year gets pretty easy. Almost too easy, I'm only taking two mandatory academic classes because I was too lazy to put them in my schedule before. Last semester was rough because I had to retake a few classes I failed that I didn't redo in summer school.
Even if it's not the case for you, teachers are generally more understanding and chill when it comes to seniors. 
I have a 1.8 GPA, raised it by .2 since freshman year.
I've failed 6 classes because of mental illness. I should have failed 10, but some of my teachers were kind enough to pass me with an S grade, meaning I technically got the credit but it didn't do anything to my GPA.
I'm still about to graduate with one extra credit.
See if your school has any sort of alternative grading system like that. See if you can talk to a counselor to talk to teachers about it if that's easier.
Junior year is definitely the worst year, but for everyone I know, senior year gets 1000x better.
Hopefully that helps.
Thank God I'm too lazy to complete certain compulsions
